Mirrors the engine\'s\n `build_neighbor_graph` binding: the count `k` is required; `min_similarity`,\n `mutual`, `exact`, and `table` are optional with explicit presence so an unset\n field resolves to the engine default rather than a literal `0`/`false`/`\"\"`.\n The engine-side build knobs `self_exclude` / `exact_max_rows` / `resolve_keys`\n are not on the wire \xe2\x80\x94 the server applies the engine defaults, the single\n source of those values.\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x04\x06\x01\x12\x04\xc1\x01\x08!\nE\n\x04\x04\x06\x02\x00\x12\x04\xc3\x01\x02\x17\x1a7 Source whose embedding table the graph is built over.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x00\x05\x12\x04\xc3\x01\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\xc3\x01\t\x12\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x00\x03\x12\x04\xc3\x01\x15\x16\n2\n\x04\x04\x06\x02\x01\x12\x04\xc5\x01\x02\x0f\x1a$ Neighbourhood size `k` (required).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x01\x05\x12\x04\xc5\x01\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\xc5\x01\t\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x01\x03\x12\x04\xc5\x01\r\x0e\nE\n\x04\x04\x06\x02\x02\x12\x04\xc7\x01\x02$\x1a7 Optional minimum cosine similarity floor for an edge.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x02\x04\x12\x04\xc7\x01\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x02\x05\x12\x04\xc7\x01\x0b\x10\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\xc7\x01\x11\x1f\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x02\x03\x12\x04\xc7\x01\"#\n+\n\x04\x04\x06\x02\x03\x12\x04\xc9\x01\x02\x12\x1a\x1d Keep only reciprocal edges.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x03\x05\x12\x04\xc9\x01\x02\x06\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x03\x01\x12\x04\xc9\x01\x07\r\n\r\n\x05\x04\x06\x02\x03\x03\x12\x04\xc9\x01\x10\x11\n\x99\x01\n\x04\x04\x06\x02\x04\x12\x04\xcc\x01\x02\x11\x1a\x8a\x01 Use the exact (deterministic, complete) driver, gated by a row-count\n ceiling; UNSPECIFIED maps to the engine default (`Bypass`). Mirrors the\n engine\'s `PropagationWeighting`; UNSPECIFIED maps to the engine default\n (`DegreeNormalized`).\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x05\x03\x01\x12\x04\xd9\x01\x05\x19\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x03\x02\x00\x12\x04\xda\x01\x02(\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\xda\x01\x02#\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x00\x02\x12\x04\xda\x01&\'\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x03\x02\x01\x12\x04\xdb\x01\x02.\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\xdb\x01\x02)\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x01\x02\x12\x04\xdb\x01,-\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x03\x02\x02\x12\x04\xdc\x01\x02$\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\xdc\x01\x02\x1f\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x02\x02\x12\x04\xdc\x01\"#\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x03\x02\x03\x12\x04\xdd\x01\x02,\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x03\x01\x12\x04\xdd\x01\x02\'\n\r\n\x05\x05\x03\x02\x03\x02\x12\x04\xdd\x01*+\n\x86\x01\n\x02\x05\x04\x12\x06\xe2\x01\x00\xe6\x01\x01\x1ax What a propagation emits. Mirrors the engine\'s `PropagationOutput`;\n UNSPECIFIED maps to the engine default (`Final`).\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x05\x04\x01\x12\x04\xe2\x01\x05\x16\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x04\x02\x00\x12\x04\xe3\x01\x02%\n\r\n\x05\x05\x04\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\xe3\x01\x02 \n\r\n\x05\x05\x04\x02\x00\x02\x12\x04\xe3\x01#$\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x04\x02\x01\x12\x04\xe4\x01\x02\x1f\n\r\n\x05\x05\x04\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\xe4\x01\x02\x1a\n\r\n\x05\x05\x04\x02\x01\x02\x12\x04\xe4\x01\x1d\x1e\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x04\x02\x02\x12\x04\xe5\x01\x02+\n\r\n\x05\x05\x04\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\xe5\x01\x02&\n\r\n\x05\x05\x04\x02\x02\x02\x12\x04\xe5\x01)*\n\xdd\x01\n\x02\x04\x07\x12\x06\xeb\x01\x00\xf4\x01\x01\x1a\xce\x01 A registered external edge source and its column bindings, for the\n `edge_source` arm of a propagation. The endpoints join to the source on the\n key; `weight_column` feeds the `edge_similarity` weighting.\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x04\x07\x01\x12\x04\xeb\x01\x08\x1b\n;\n\x04\x04\x07\x02\x00\x12\x04\xed\x01\x02\x19\x1a- Registered source id holding the edge rows.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x00\x05\x12\x04\xed\x01\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\xed\x01\t\x14\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x00\x03\x12\x04\xed\x01\x17\x18\nU\n\x04\x04\x07\x02\x01\x12\x04\xef\x01\x02\x18\x1aG Column holding the edge\'s source endpoint (default \"src\" when empty).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x01\x05\x12\x04\xef\x01\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\xef\x01\t\x13\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x01\x03\x12\x04\xef\x01\x16\x17\nZ\n\x04\x04\x07\x02\x02\x12\x04\xf1\x01\x02\x18\x1aL Column holding the edge\'s destination endpoint (default \"dst\" when empty).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x02\x05\x12\x04\xf1\x01\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\xf1\x01\t\x13\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x02\x03\x12\x04\xf1\x01\x16\x17\n8\n\x04\x04\x07\x02\x03\x12\x04\xf3\x01\x02$\x1a* Optional column holding the edge weight.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x03\x04\x12\x04\xf3\x01\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x03\x05\x12\x04\xf3\x01\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x03\x01\x12\x04\xf3\x01\x12\x1f\n\r\n\x05\x04\x07\x02\x03\x03\x12\x04\xf3\x01\"#\n\xc8\x03\n\x02\x04\x08\x12\x06\xfc\x01\x00\x98\x02\x01\x1a\xb9\x03 Propagate an embedding table\'s features over a declared graph. Mirrors the\n engine\'s `propagate_embeddings` binding. The graph is either an S9 similarity\n graph (`edge_graph_table`, a `build_neighbor_graph` output) or a registered\n external edge source (`edge_source`) \xe2\x80\x94 exactly one, modelled as a `oneof` so\n both/neither is a decode error. The optional scalars carry explicit presence\n so an unset field resolves to the engine default.\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x04\x08\x01\x12\x04\xfc\x01\x08\"\nS\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x00\x12\x04\xfe\x01\x02\x17\x1aE Source whose embedding table holds the input features `X\xe2\x81\xbd\xe2\x81\xb0\xe2\x81\xbe`.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x00\x05\x12\x04\xfe\x01\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\xfe\x01\t\x12\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x00\x03\x12\x04\xfe\x01\x15\x16\nW\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x01\x12\x04\x80\x02\x02&\x1aI Optional specific embedding table; unset resolves the source\'s default.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x01\x04\x12\x04\x80\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x01\x05\x12\x04\x80\x02\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\x80\x02\x12!\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x01\x03\x12\x04\x80\x02$%\nB\n\x04\x04\x08\x08\x00\x12\x06\x82\x02\x02\x87\x02\x03\x1a2 The graph to propagate over \xe2\x80\x94 exactly one arm.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x08\x00\x01\x12\x04\x82\x02\x08\r\nT\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x02\x12\x04\x84\x02\x04 \x1aF An S9 similarity graph (a `build_neighbor_graph` output table name).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x02\x05\x12\x04\x84\x02\x04\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\x84\x02\x0b\x1b\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x02\x03\x12\x04\x84\x02\x1e\x1f\nH\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x03\x12\x04\x86\x02\x04(\x1a: A registered external edge source + its column bindings.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x03\x06\x12\x04\x86\x02\x04\x17\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x03\x01\x12\x04\x86\x02\x18#\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x03\x03\x12\x04\x86\x02&\'\nu\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x04\x12\x04\x8a\x02\x021\x1ag Edge direction read when building the neighbourhood. UNSPECIFIED maps to the\n engine default (`Out`).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x04\x06\x12\x04\x8a\x02\x02\"\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x04\x01\x12\x04\x8a\x02#,\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x04\x03\x12\x04\x8a\x02/0\nC\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x05\x12\x04\x8c\x02\x02\x1b\x1a5 Optional hop count (clamped to the engine hop cap).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x05\x04\x12\x04\x8c\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x05\x05\x12\x04\x8c\x02\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x05\x01\x12\x04\x8c\x02\x12\x16\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x05\x03\x12\x04\x8c\x02\x19\x1a\n1\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x06\x12\x04\x8e\x02\x02%\x1a# Neighbour-contribution weighting.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x06\x06\x12\x04\x8e\x02\x02\x16\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x06\x01\x12\x04\x8e\x02\x17 \n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x06\x03\x12\x04\x8e\x02#$\n4\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x07\x12\x04\x90\x02\x02\x1c\x1a& Optional APPNP teleport probability.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x07\x04\x12\x04\x90\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x07\x05\x12\x04\x90\x02\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x07\x01\x12\x04\x90\x02\x12\x17\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x07\x03\x12\x04\x90\x02\x1a\x1b\n+\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\x08\x12\x04\x92\x02\x02\x1f\x1a\x1d What the propagation emits.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x08\x06\x12\x04\x92\x02\x02\x13\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x08\x01\x12\x04\x92\x02\x14\x1a\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\x08\x03\x12\x04\x92\x02\x1d\x1e\n\x80\x02\n\x04\x04\x08\x02\t\x12\x04\x97\x02\x02,\x1a\xf1\x01 Opt-in memoization. UNSPECIFIED maps to the engine default (`Bypass`). A\n propagation is anchored on the immutable source-embedding-table and\n edge-relation digests, so it is genuinely cacheable: a `Use` request reuses\n an exact prior run.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\t\x06\x12\x04\x97\x02\x02 \n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\t\x01\x12\x04\x97\x02!&\n\r\n\x05\x04\x08\x02\t\x03\x12\x04\x97\x02)+\n\xb3\x01\n\x02\x05\x05\x12\x06\x9d\x02\x00\xa2\x02\x01\x1a\xa4\x01 Which permutation-invariant reduction the context-set encoder pools with.\n Mirrors the engine\'s `SetAggregator`; UNSPECIFIED maps to the engine default\n (`Mean`).\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x05\x05\x01\x12\x04\x9d\x02\x05\x12\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x05\x02\x00\x12\x04\x9e\x02\x02!\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\x9e\x02\x02\x1c\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x00\x02\x12\x04\x9e\x02\x1f \n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x05\x02\x01\x12\x04\x9f\x02\x02\x1a\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\x9f\x02\x02\x15\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x01\x02\x12\x04\x9f\x02\x18\x19\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x05\x02\x02\x12\x04\xa0\x02\x02\x19\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\xa0\x02\x02\x14\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x02\x02\x12\x04\xa0\x02\x17\x18\n\x0c\n\x04\x05\x05\x02\x03\x12\x04\xa1\x02\x02\x19\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x03\x01\x12\x04\xa1\x02\x02\x14\n\r\n\x05\x05\x05\x02\x03\x02\x12\x04\xa1\x02\x17\x18\n\xb5\x02\n\x02\x04\t\x12\x06\xa8\x02\x00\xc5\x02\x01\x1a\xa6\x02 Assemble and encode a target\'s context set. Mirrors the engine\'s\n `assemble_context` binding. `query` is the target\'s vector; an absent\n `edges` block is the ANN-only default, a present block (without `hybrid`) is a\n declared-edge walk, and a present block with `hybrid` is the union of both.\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x04\t\x01\x12\x04\xa8\x02\x08\x1e\n\x87\x01\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x00\x12\x04\xab\x02\x02\x17\x1ay Source whose embedding table the context is retrieved against and whose rows\n the members are pooled and hydrated from.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x00\x05\x12\x04\xab\x02\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\xab\x02\t\x12\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x00\x03\x12\x04\xab\x02\x15\x16\n\x97\x01\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x01\x12\x04\xae\x02\x02\x1b\x1a\x88\x01 The target\'s query vector \xe2\x80\x94 the point whose neighbourhood is the context.\n IEEE-754 `float` (bit-exact for the engine\'s `Vec<f32>`).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x01\x04\x12\x04\xae\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x01\x05\x12\x04\xae\x02\x0b\x10\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\xae\x02\x11\x16\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x01\x03\x12\x04\xae\x02\x19\x1a\n\'\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x02\x12\x04\xb0\x02\x02\x0f\x1a\x19 Neighbourhood size `k`.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x02\x05\x12\x04\xb0\x02\x02\x08\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\xb0\x02\t\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x02\x03\x12\x04\xb0\x02\r\x0e\nP\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x03\x12\x04\xb2\x02\x02$\x1aB Optional label/outcome columns hydrated for each context member.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x03\x04\x12\x04\xb2\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x03\x05\x12\x04\xb2\x02\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x03\x01\x12\x04\xb2\x02\x12\x1f\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x03\x03\x12\x04\xb2\x02\"#\n&\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x04\x12\x04\xb4\x02\x02\x1f\x1a\x18 The pooling reduction.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x04\x06\x12\x04\xb4\x02\x02\x0f\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x04\x01\x12\x04\xb4\x02\x10\x1a\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x04\x03\x12\x04\xb4\x02\x1d\x1e\n\xd9\x02\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x05\x12\x04\xba\x02\x02!\x1a\xca\x02 Drop the target\'s own row (`exclude_key`) before pooling \xe2\x80\x94 the leakage\n guard. Explicit presence: an unset field resolves to the engine default\n (`true`), the single source of that value, so a client that omits it keeps\n the leakage guard on rather than silently disabling it via the proto3 bare-\n bool wire default (`false`).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x05\x04\x12\x04\xba\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x05\x05\x12\x04\xba\x02\x0b\x0f\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x05\x01\x12\x04\xba\x02\x10\x1c\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x05\x03\x12\x04\xba\x02\x1f \nU\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x06\x12\x04\xbc\x02\x02\"\x1aG Optional target row key dropped from the context when `exclude_self`.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x06\x04\x12\x04\xbc\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x06\x05\x12\x04\xbc\x02\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x06\x01\x12\x04\xbc\x02\x12\x1d\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x06\x03\x12\x04\xbc\x02 !\nF\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x07\x12\x04\xbe\x02\x02\x1c\x1a8 Optional SQL predicate scoping the context to a split.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x07\x04\x12\x04\xbe\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x07\x05\x12\x04\xbe\x02\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x07\x01\x12\x04\xbe\x02\x12\x17\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x07\x03\x12\x04\xbe\x02\x1a\x1b\n\x94\x01\n\x04\x04\t\x02\x08\x12\x04\xc1\x02\x023\x1a\x85\x01 Optional declared-edge gather. Absent = ANN-only; present = declared-edge\n walk, or (with `hybrid`) the union with the ANN context.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x08\x04\x12\x04\xc1\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x08\x06\x12\x04\xc1\x02\x0b(\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x08\x01\x12\x04\xc1\x02).\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\x08\x03\x12\x04\xc1\x0212\n_\n\x04\x04\t\x02\t\x12\x04\xc4\x02\x02\x13\x1aQ Union the declared-edge and ANN candidate sets (only meaningful with\n `edges`).\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\t\x05\x12\x04\xc4\x02\x02\x06\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\t\x01\x12\x04\xc4\x02\x07\r\n\r\n\x05\x04\t\x02\t\x03\x12\x04\xc4\x02\x10\x12\n\xe9\x02\n\x02\x04\n\x12\x06\xcc\x02\x00\xcf\x02\x01\x1a\xda\x02 The pooled fixed-width context vector. A wrapper message (carried as an\n `optional` field) so a degenerate empty context (`None` \xe2\x80\x94 no neighbour\n survived exclusion/split) is distinguishable from a present-but-empty vector:\n the absence is a correctness signal a decoder reads as low-confidence, never\n silently averaged into a representation.\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x04\n\x01\x12\x04\xcc\x02\x08\x15\nI\n\x04\x04\n\x02\x00\x12\x04\xce\x02\x02\x1c\x1a; The pooled vector `\xcf\x81(\xce\xa3 \xcf\x86(x\xe1\xb5\xa2))`, in IEEE-754 `float`.\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\n\x02\x00\x04\x12\x04\xce\x02\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\n\x02\x00\x05\x12\x04\xce\x02\x0b\x10\n\r\n\x05\x04\n\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\xce\x02\x11\x17\n\r\n\x05\x04\n\x02\x00\x03\x12\x04\xce\x02\x1a\x1b\n\xea\x01\n\x02\x04\x0b\x12\x06\xd4\x02\x00\xe3\x02\x01\x1a\xdb\x01 Result of one AssembleContext invocation. TrainingService \xe2\x80\x94 the wire surface for the engine\'s training verbs.\n\n `StartTraining` and `TrainingStatus` are imperative session methods, not SQL\n queries, so they live as typed gRPC RPCs alongside SessionService /\n TriggerService / EmbeddingService / InferenceService / EvalService rather\n than on the Flight SQL surface (which carries query/result only, per ADR-01\n \xc2\xa73.2). Training is a substrate primitive \xe2\x80\x94 meta-learning an adapter or a\n predictor over a registered source \xe2\x80\x94 and names no tenant-domain concept.\n\n The service serves all three engine training kinds (`fine_tune`,\n `graph_fine_tune`, `context_predictor`) behind one verb: `StartTraining`\n carries a full `TrainingSpec` oneof and dispatches to the matching engine\n submit verb, returning the durable job id and the (deterministic) output\n model id. The job runs asynchronously inside the engine; the client polls\n `TrainingStatus` by id until a terminal state. There is no progress stream \xe2\x80\x94\n the abstraction exposes none, so this surface invents none. The service\n reimplements no training, LoRA, sampling, or scan logic; it is purely a wire\n adapter.\n\n Tenant scope is read from the request\'s `SessionTenant` extension, set by the\n shared TenantInterceptor from the `jammi-session-id` header \xe2\x80\x94 the same\n mechanism every other gRPC service and Flight SQL already use.\n\n\n\n\x03\x06\x00\x01\x12\x03\x1c\x08\x17\n\xb3\x02\n\x04\x06\x00\x02\x00\x12\x03!\x02J\x1a\xa5\x02 Submit a training job over a registered source and return its id + output\n model id. The job trains asynchronously; poll `TrainingStatus` with the\n returned job id. Peer of the engine\'s `fine_tune` / `fine_tune_graph` /\n `train_context_predictor` submit verbs (the spec oneof selects which).\n\n\x0c\n\x05\x06\x00\x02\x00\x01\x12\x03!\x06\x13\n\x0c\n\x05\x06\x00\x02\x00\x02\x12\x03!\x14(\n\x0c\n\x05\x06\x00\x02\x00\x03\x12\x03!3H\n\xa1\x02\n\x04\x06\x00\x02\x01\x12\x03\'\x02M\x1a\x93\x02 Read a training job\'s current status by id, plus its output model id and\n the failure message when it failed. When `mine` is set the trainer mines hard negatives\n from its own ANN index, excluding the positive\'s `exclude_hops`-hop\n neighbourhood and re-mining every `refresh_every` epochs.\n\n As with `FineTuneConfig`, every scalar knob is `optional` so an unset field\n is distinguishable from a legal `0`: the server reads an unset field as\n \"apply the engine default\" (`HardNegativeConfig::default()`) and a present\n field as an override. A caller that sets only `mine = true` therefore ships\n the engine\'s `k`/`exclude_hops`/`refresh_every` defaults rather than zeros,\n which `FineTuneConfig::validate` would otherwise reject.\n\n\x0b\n\x03\x04\x03\x01\x12\x04\x9b\x01\x08\x1a\n\x0c\n\x04\x04\x03\x02\x00\x12\x04\x9c\x01\x02\x10\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x00\x05\x12\x04\x9c\x01\x02\x06\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x00\x01\x12\x04\x9c\x01\x07\x0b\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x00\x03\x12\x04\x9c\x01\x0e\x0f\n\x0c\n\x04\x04\x03\x02\x01\x12\x04\x9d\x01\x02\x18\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x01\x04\x12\x04\x9d\x01\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x01\x05\x12\x04\x9d\x01\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x01\x01\x12\x04\x9d\x01\x12\x13\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x01\x03\x12\x04\x9d\x01\x16\x17\n\x0c\n\x04\x04\x03\x02\x02\x12\x04\x9e\x01\x02#\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x02\x04\x12\x04\x9e\x01\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x02\x05\x12\x04\x9e\x01\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x02\x01\x12\x04\x9e\x01\x12\x1e\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x02\x03\x12\x04\x9e\x01!\"\n\x0c\n\x04\x04\x03\x02\x03\x12\x04\x9f\x01\x02$\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x03\x04\x12\x04\x9f\x01\x02\n\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x03\x05\x12\x04\x9f\x01\x0b\x11\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x03\x01\x12\x04\x9f\x01\x12\x1f\n\r\n\x05\x04\x03\x02\x03\x03\x12\x04\x9f\x01\"#\n\xae\x05\n\x02\x04\x04\x12\x06\xab\x01\x00\xdb\x01\x01\x1a\x9f\x05 Configuration for a fine-tuning job. Mirrors the engine\'s `FineTuneConfig`\n field for field; every field is read by the trainer or the LoRA builder.\n Every scalar knob is `optional` so an unset field is distinguishable from a\n legal `0`/`false`: the server reads an unset field as \"apply the engine\n default\" (`FineTuneConfig::default()`) and a present field as an override,\n making the engine the single source of default values. `embedding_loss`/\n `classification_loss` are unset to let the engine auto-select from the data\n format; `layers_to_transform` is unset for \"all layers\". AuditService \xe2\x80\x94 the wire surface for the engine\'s per-query audit verbs.\n\n `AuditLog`, `AuditFetchByQueryId`, and `AuditFetchRecent` are imperative\n session methods \xe2\x80\x94 signing, tenant-injection, and signature-verified decode\n are non-SQL logic \xe2\x80\x94 so they live as typed gRPC RPCs alongside the other\n engine-backed services rather than on the Flight SQL surface (query/result\n only, per ADR-01 \xc2\xa73.2). The verbs name a substrate primitive \xe2\x80\x94 a signed\n per-query audit log \xe2\x80\x94 and carry no tenant-domain concept.\n\n Each verb delegates 1:1 to the consumer-facing `Session`\n abstraction (`audit_log` / `audit_fetch_by_query_id` / `audit_fetch_recent`);\n the service reimplements no signing, storage, or query logic. The\n `PerQueryAudit` message mirrors the Rust record field for field, including\n its server-computed `signature`.\n\n Tenant scope is read from the request\'s `SessionTenant` extension, set by the\n shared TenantInterceptor. The audit primitive requires a bound tenant \xe2\x80\x94 an\n unscoped call is rejected by the engine.\n\n\n\n\x03\x06\x00\x01\x12\x03\x18\x08\x14\n\xa1\x01\n\x04\x06\x00\x02\x00\x12\x03\x1b\x02@\x1a\x93\x01 Sign and persist a batch of audit records under the session\'s tenant,\n publishing them to the audit topic. rpc cannot escape coverage by being forgotten in a constant.

# AuditErrorDetail in jammi_wire::proto::error - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-wire/0.32.1/jammi_wire/proto/error/struct.AuditErrorDetail.html

## Expand description

AuditErrorDetail — the structured wire detail for `jammi_db::AuditError`,
attached to a `tonic::Status` by the server’s `map_audit_error` so a remote
the data-plane client reconstructs the EXACT `AuditError` the in-process path
returns.

Every owned-shape variant has its own typed arm and reconstructs faithfully.
The only fold is `serde` — `AuditError::Serde(#\[from\] serde_json::Error)`
wraps a foreign error that cannot cross a process boundary, so it carries its
faithful `Display` string (the genuine fidelity limit, mirroring how
`JammiErrorDetail` folds its own foreign `#\[from\]` variants).

with no variant reconstructs as an empty `Storage`.

# JammiErrorDetail in jammi_wire::proto::error - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-wire/0.32.1/jammi_wire/proto/error/struct.JammiErrorDetail.html

## Expand description

JammiErrorDetail — the structured domain-error payload a server attaches to
a `tonic::Status` so a remote client can reconstruct the EXACT engine
`JammiError` the in-process path returns, not a lossy gRPC-code-category
guess. Carried in the Status `details` bytes (the gRPC richer-error model);
the Status `code` + `message` still hold the idiomatic gRPC surface for
clients that do not decode the detail.

The standard gRPC code set is insufficient to distinguish the engine’s
failure modes — `invalid_argument` alone collapses Source / Model / Tenant /
Config / Schema / Eval into one code — so a typed detail payload is the
ADR-01 §5.3-sanctioned mechanism for “structured error information when the
standard gRPC code set is insufficient”. A typed `oneof` (not a
`google.rpc.Any`) keeps it type-driven: each engine variant reachable on the
embedding/search verb surface has its own message carrying exactly the
fields needed to reconstruct it.

The contract is complete over `JammiError`: every owned-shape variant — the
String- and struct-carrying ones whose fields fully reconstruct the variant —
has its own typed arm here. `MutableTable` and `ChannelCatalog` are NOT
folded: their inner errors (`MutableTableError`, `ChannelCatalogError`) are
engine-owned (every field reconstructs), so they carry their own structured
detail (`MutableTableErrorDetail`, `ChannelCatalogErrorDetail`) and
reconstruct faithfully — the same standard the owned-shape variants meet. The
only variants folded into `other` are the genuinely-foreign `#\[from\]` ones whose inner error
cannot cross a process boundary (`Io`/`std::io::Error`,
`BackendDriver`/`Toml`/`Json`/`DataFusion`/`Trigger`/`Storage`): they
reconstruct as `JammiError::Other` carrying the faithful `Display` string —
the genuine fidelity limit, not a lossy guess. Faithfulness is a property of
the error type, so the mapping covers the whole enum, not only one verb
surface.

# TriggerErrorDetail in jammi_wire::proto::error - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-wire/0.32.1/jammi_wire/proto/error/struct.TriggerErrorDetail.html

## Expand description

TriggerErrorDetail — the structured wire detail for `jammi_db::TriggerError`,
attached to a `tonic::Status` by the server’s `map_trigger_error` so a remote
the data-plane client reconstructs the EXACT `TriggerError` the in-process path
returns (the standard gRPC code set collapses several variants onto one code).

The contract is complete and faithful over `TriggerError`. Every owned-shape
variant has its own typed arm. The two `#\[from\]` variants do NOT fold: their
inner errors are engine-owned and fully reconstructable, so `backing_table`
nests the shared `MutableTableErrorDetail` and `backend` nests the shared
`BackendErrorDetail` — the same faithful taxonomies `JammiErrorDetail` reuses.
No `TriggerError` variant degrades to a lossy string.

# CalibrationShape in jammi_wire::proto::eval - Rust

```
#[repr(i32)]pub enum CalibrationShape {
    Unspecified = 0,
    Gaussian = 1,
    Sample = 2,
}
```
## Expand description

The predictive output shape an `eval_calibration` golden source carries.
Mirrors the engine’s `EvalCalibrationShape`: the shape selects which columns
the runner reads and which scoring family scores them.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unspecified)

### Unspecified = 0

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Gaussian)

### Gaussian = 1

A parametric predictive `Normal(mean, sd)`: the source carries `mean`,
`sd`, and `outcome` numeric columns.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Sample)

### Sample = 2

An ensemble of predictive draws: the source carries a `draws` column (a
JSON array per row) and an `outcome` numeric column.

# EvalCalibrationShape in jammi_wire::eval - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-wire/0.32.1/jammi_wire/eval/enum.EvalCalibrationShape.html

```
pub enum EvalCalibrationShape {
    Gaussian,
    Sample,
}
```
## Expand description

The predictive output shape an `eval_calibration` golden source carries.

A calibration golden source pairs a held-out predictive distribution with
its realised outcome. The shape selects which columns the runner reads and
which proper-score / diagnostic family scores them — exactly the way
[ EvalTask](https://docs.rs/enum.EvalTask.html) selects the inference metric. Both families are scored on the
same yardstick (CRPS / NLL / PIT-calibration / sharpness), so a parametric
(NP3) and an ensemble (NP4) predictor are directly comparable.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Gaussian)

### Gaussian

A parametric predictive `Normal(mean, sd)`: the source carries `mean`,
`sd`, and `outcome` numeric columns.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Sample)

### Sample

An ensemble of predictive draws: the source carries a `draws` column (a
JSON array of numbers per row) and an `outcome` numeric column.

Matches `train_embedding_model.py` which uses `AdamW(weight_decay=0.01)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.max_grad_norm)

`max_grad_norm: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)Maximum global L2 norm for gradient clipping. `0.0` disables clipping.
Default: 1.0. Matches `train_embedding_model.py` which uses
`torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, max_norm=1.0)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.cached)

`cached: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)GradCache: compute the in-batch-negative loss in two passes so the
effective negative pool is the whole batch without holding every
representation’s activation graph at once. A no-grad pass embeds all
rows and caches each representation’s loss-gradient; a second pass
re-embeds chunk by chunk with grad and backpropagates through the
cached gradient, freeing each chunk’s graph before the next. The
optimiser sees the same gradient as a single-pass run (a tolerance test
pins this), but peak memory scales with the chunk, not the batch.
Distinct from `gradient_accumulation_steps`, which does *not* enlarge
the in-batch negative pool. Only applies to the in-batch-negative
objective (`MultipleNegativesRanking`). Default: `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.hard_negatives)

`hard_negatives: `[HardNegativeConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.HardNegativeConfig.html)Hard-negative mining configuration. With `mine = true` the trainer
mines hard negatives from its own ANN index (see [ HardNegativeConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.HardNegativeConfig.html)).
Default: mining off.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.matryoshka_dims)

`matryoshka_dims: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>Matryoshka representation dimensions. When non-empty, the embedding
objective is evaluated at each listed prefix dimension and the losses
summed, so the leading coordinates of the embedding carry the most
information and a consumer can truncate the served vector to any listed
dimension with graceful quality decay. Importance-ordering is *created*
by training with this on, so truncation at serve time is only valid for
a model trained with these dims. Empty (default) trains the full
dimension only. Each entry must be `> 0` and `<=` the embedding width.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.seed)

`seed: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)Random seed for the fine-tune. The LoRA A/B initialisation and the
dropout mask are a pure function of this seed and each parameter’s name,
so on `Device::Cpu` two runs with the same `(seed, source rows, config)`
produce byte-identical adapter weights — run-to-run and across processes.
Fixed per job (never drawn from entropy at construction); the default
[ DEFAULT_FINE_TUNE_SEED](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_FINE_TUNE_SEED.html) is used when a caller does not specify one.

The engine is the single source of default values: decode starts from
[ FineTuneConfig::default()](https://docs.rs/struct.FineTuneConfig.html#method.default) and overrides a field only when the wire
carries it. Each scalar knob has explicit presence (

`optional`), so an unset
field is distinguishable from a legal `0`/`false` and resolves to the engine
default rather than a literal zero. The optional loss messages map to
`Option<…Loss>` (unset → engine auto-selects from the data format). The
enum-typed fields fall back to the engine default variant when left
`UNSPECIFIED`. A config that sets only a handful of knobs behaves exactly
like `FineTuneConfig::default()` for the rest.## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

# decode_ipc_schema in jammi_wire - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-wire/0.32.1/jammi_wire/fn.decode_ipc_schema.html

## Expand description

Decode an Arrow IPC stream’s schema message into a [ SchemaRef](https://docs.rs/arrow-schema/57.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/arrow_schema/schema/type.SchemaRef.html). The bytes
are a self-describing IPC stream (a

`schema` message, optionally followed by
batches) — the same framing [produces; a schema-only payload is](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_ipc_stream.html)

`encode_ipc_stream``encode_ipc_stream(schema, &[])`. Used by the verbs that carry a
table/topic schema declaration on the wire rather than a batch of rows.

# decode_publish_batch in jammi_wire - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-wire/0.32.1/jammi_wire/fn.decode_publish_batch.html

```
pub fn decode_publish_batch(
    wire: &
```
[ArrowBatch](https://docs.rs/proto/trigger/struct.ArrowBatch.html),
    topic: &[TopicDefinition](https://docs.rs/jammi-db/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jammi_db/trigger/topic/struct.TopicDefinition.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RecordBatch](https://docs.rs/arrow-array/57.3.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/arrow_array/record_batch/struct.RecordBatch.html), [Status](https://docs.rs/tonic/0.14.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tonic/status/struct.Status.html)>## Expand description

Decode the single record batch a `Publish` carries, checking it against the
topic schema. Per ADR-01 §5.1 the wire pairing is `data_header` +
`data_body`; the shared decoder concatenates them and reads the IPC stream. A
publish carries exactly one batch — an empty or multi-batch payload is a
typed client error, and a schema mismatch is rejected so a malformed publish
never partially writes.

`encode_delivered_batch`A batch carries exactly one record batch (the publish unit); an absent or
multi-batch payload is a corrupt frame, surfaced as an `Err` so the stream’s
item is a faithful failure rather than a fabricated batch. The offset’s
`committed_at` is set to `produced_at` — the two are the same instant by the
broker’s contract (see [ DeliveredBatch](https://docs.rs/jammi-db/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jammi_db/trigger/subscription/struct.DeliveredBatch.html)).

# DerivesFromEdge in jammi_db::store::freshness - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jammi-db/0.32.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jammi_db/store/freshness/struct.DerivesFromEdge.html

```
pub struct DerivesFromEdge {
    pub input:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub derived: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub kind: [AnchorKind](https://docs.rs/manifest/enum.AnchorKind.html),
}## Expand description

One reverse-dependency edge of the materialization lineage: `derived`
anchored on `input` (with anchor kind `kind`), so a change to `input`
propagates to `derived`. Returned one hop at a time by
[ ResultStore::derives_from](https://docs.rs/struct.ResultStore.html#method.derives_from); a caller walks the relation transitively.

The lineage is a *view over* the recorded `input_anchors_json` — the single
source of truth — not a second edge store: an edge exists iff some `ready`
table’s manifest summary records `input` as a source.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.input)

`input: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The upstream input source the edge points *from*.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.derived)

`derived: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The downstream table that anchored on `input`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.kind)

`kind: `[AnchorKind](https://docs.rs/manifest/enum.AnchorKind.html)The kind of anchor `derived` recorded for `input`.
